subject.title: fix(config): bound state-directory .env file reads with size limit

question: Should OpenClaw intentionally treat existing state-directory and global runtime `.env` files larger than 1 MiB as invalid and continue startup without loading their variables?
rationale: The patch is mechanically coherent, but this is a deliberate compatibility boundary for existing operator-managed startup configuration rather than a purely internal implementation detail.

options.title: Accept the 1 MiB boundary
options.body: Merge with the documented behavior that oversized dotenv files are skipped and warned about, preserving startup availability and bounded memory use.

options.title: Choose a different compatibility contract
options.body: Ask for a different cap or migration/diagnostic approach if OpenClaw must continue supporting unusually large existing dotenv files.

recommendation.title: Accept the 1 MiB boundary
recommendation.body: Merge with the documented behavior that oversized dotenv files are skipped and warned about, preserving startup availability and bounded memory use.

likelyOwner.reason: They identified the shared startup-path requirement and are currently assigned to review this exact compatibility tradeoff.
